newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids flat in thin, pre-holiday trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids flat in thin, pre-holiday trading.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices were flat Tuesday from Monday in light, pre-holiday trading as most participants were absent in observance of the Christmas holiday.
Spot domestic demand for fuel oil remained sparse amid mild weather following last week's freeze and retrenchment in swing natural gas prices after recent highs.
Nevertheless, suppliers remained hopefully resid usage will pick up as the peak of the winter season approaches and gas prices stay at higher-than-normal historical levels, said market sources.
New York Harbor one pct sulphur grade remained at $21.50-$21.75 with January one pct paper at $21.25-$21.75.
High sulphurs in New York harbor market stayed unchanged with 2.2 percent at $17.75. NYH 0.3 percent high pour grade was pegged at $22.50-$23.00.
U.S. Gulf Coast one percent stayed near $18.63, while three percent was steady at $15.50-$16.00. January three pct paper was still assessed at $16.50-$16.60.
New York city gate gas slipped to $4.10-$4.16/mmBtu in very thin activity, down from $4.28-$4.30 Monday but higher than NYH one percent resid at a $3.43/mmBtu equivalent.
